jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, AI Products & Agentic Hospitality (f/m/d)
jobs.sourceName: Jobicy: latest jobs
jobs.description:
About the role

At Apaleo , we're building the open, API-first property management platform for hospitality. With integrations across hundreds of apps through the Apaleo Store, and the first AI agent marketplace for hospitality in our Agent Hub, we simplify operations, elevate the guest journey and drive revenue growth for our customers.

We're looking for a senior Product Manager to ownin our AI product domain. You'll turn our AI capabilities into coherent, commercially viable products that solve real operational problems for hoteliers. Your goal is to help hotels move towards genuinely autonomous operations, not to ship isolated automations or AI assistants.

This is not a backlog role. You'll take an ambiguous opportunity, find the right customer problems, define the proposition, build it with Engineering, bring it to market and drive adoption. You'll also play a central role in turning our AI capabilities into a meaningful and growing source of revenue.

This is a senior individual contributor role with real autonomy. You won't receive a roadmap and execute it. You'll shape it along our vision, using customer insight, data and sound reasoning. You’ll work closely with Engineering, Design, Sales, Marketing and Customer Success, and in close collaboration with our other value stream teams.

What you'll be up to

• Productising and commercialising our AI capabilities . Define the proposition, target customers and use cases, and shape packaging and launch with commercial teams.

• Building the foundations for AI across our ecosystem. Shape how our AI capabilities understand each hotel's context and work reliably with Apaleo and connected systems across operational areas.

• Productising hospitality knowledge. Turn hospitality expertise and operational processes into scalable product experiences, with appropriate human oversight.

• Driving autonomy and measurable value. Think in complete outcomes, such as staff hours saved and manual work removed. Show hoteliers tangible ROI.

• Driving adoption. Run discovery, shape onboarding and usability, measure adoption and improve from real-world feedback.

• Keeping AI products reliable and viable. Define good agent performance, understand cost and latency, set up evaluation and monitoring with Engineering, and trade off autonomy, reliability, human intervention and cost.

• Owning strategy, roadmap and delivery in your scope , with clear specs, a definition of done and impact analysis.

• Working with Engineering on trade-offs, dependencies, quality and our API-first AI-first architecture.

• Balancing ambition with reality. Weigh the roadmap against operational requests, bugs and technical debt, and say no to good ideas that aren't great ones.

• Spotting dependencies early with Hotel Operations and other engineering teams, since our AI capabilities build on the core platform.

• Using AI in your own PM work and championing AI-assisted engineering.

What you'll bring

• 6+ years as a Product Manager, owning products from discovery through launch and adoption with limited day-to-day direction.

• Proven zero-to-one experience. You've taken a new B2B product, not a feature, from an ambiguous problem to paying customers, driving discovery, validation, definition, prioritisation and launch.

• Ownership after launch. You've owned a revenue, adoption or retention number and can tell us what moved and what you killed, pivoted or repriced.

• Commercial thinking. You've defined propositions, packaging and pricing, validated willingness to pay and worked with Sales, Marketing and Customer Success on go-to-market.

• Systems and process thinking. You break processes into steps, decisions and handoffs, and understand how systems with different data models and sources of truth affect the reliability of agents.

• Meaningful AI product experience. You've built and launched AI-powered products or capabilities used by real customers, understand what makes a product agentic, and can discuss context, tools, latency, cost and evaluation, with a view on human-in-the-loop design.

• Customer centricity and product judgement. You turn interview patterns into opportunities, make tough trade-offs and prioritise ruthlessly.

• Platform thinking. You weigh customer needs against reusable capabilities, API consistency and long-term platform evolution.

• Stakeholder alignment. You align Engineering, commercial teams and peers, manage cross-team dependencies and communicate trade-offs with confidence.

• Autonomy and adaptability. You take ownership, raise risks early and make progress through ambiguity.

Strongly preferred

• Agentic AI products in production. You've taken an agentic AI product beyond prototype to paying customers, and dealt with reliability, permissions, exceptions, human intervention and evaluation. This is different from AI-powered features such as chatbots, summarisation or copilots.

Nice to have

• Hospitality technology or hotel operations experience.

About Bobbie

Bobbie makes European-style organic infant formula manufactured end-to-end in the U.S., because we believe every parent deserves to feed their baby with confidence, without judgment and without compromise. No mystery ingredients. No shortcuts. Just clean, thoughtfully made formula that parents can trust.

But Bobbie has never been just a formula company. When the 2022 national infant formula shortage left parents across the country unable to feed their babies, we closed our storefront to new customers rather than leave a single existing family without formula. We went to Washington. We got loud. And we opened our Heath, Ohio manufacturing facility to make sure something like that could never happen again.

That's who we are, and that's what you'd be joining.

Bobbie for Change

Our advocacy arm, Bobbie for Change, exists because making great formula isn't enough if the systems around parenthood are still broken. We fight for paid federal parental leave, push for legislation to prevent future formula shortages, advocate for feeding equity, and support families navigating impossible situations, including donating formula to parents impacted by breast and gynecologic cancers through the Bobbie Breasties program.

We're a company that genuinely believes becoming a parent makes you an activist. The people who work here feel that too.

As the Director of Innovation on Bobbie’s New Ventures team reporting to the President, New Ventures, you will help build the next chapters of Bobbie’s growth by identifying and launching new categories, products, formats, and business models that expand where and how we can serve families. Your job is to answer: Where should Bobbie play next? What should we build? And have we proven it deserves to scale? Once an innovation has demonstrated strong consumer demand and a viable path to scale, you will lead the transition into Bobbie’s core studio for ongoing brand management and growth.

jobs.title: Release Strategist, Professional Services
jobs.sourceName: Jobicy: latest jobs
jobs.description:
About the Job:

Most companies don’t have a “release problem” so much as a way-of-working problem. Shipping live functionality to their customers takes too long, depends on a few heroes, or happens with fingers crossed, and AI-assisted development is raising the stakes. LaunchDarkly Professional Services is helping our most strategic customers change that, and we’re hiring a Release Strategist to lead those engagements.

As a Release Strategist on LaunchDarkly's Professional Services team, you are the “product manager” for each customer engagement, responsible for defining how that customer achieves release excellence by evolving their software and agentic release processes. You join the sales cycle early to define the problem and quantify what it’s costing them, then own the engagement through delivery and adoption until the change sticks. You own the “why” and the “what”; our Solutions Architects, who serve as our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), own the “how.”

Day to day, you’ll partner with a Solutions Architect on each engagement, combining their technical judgment with your view of the commercial context, customer priorities, and relationship dynamics. Neither of you can do the job alone. You own the problem, the value, the scope, and the success criteria; your Solutions Architect owns the technical approach and its quality. You’ll also work closely with Account Executives and Customer Success Managers, and you’ll lead without direct authority, so influence, clarity, and trust matter more than title.

This is a new role, and its shape will flex and adapt as the business grows. Early on, expect to lean into scoping, delivery, and change leadership on both the pre-sales and post-sales side of the business. As we establish a feedback loop through customer delivery, you’ll extend that product mindset from individual engagements to our offerings themselves, and help write the playbook for how we package engagements, measure success, and bring on the next Release Strategist.

Responsibilities:

• Product & Value

• Scope the problem and the value if solved: join sales cycles from early discovery, map the customer’s organization and decision landscape, and quantify the business value of their release and delivery problem.

• Define the customer engagement like a product: identify the business challenges and, with your Solutions Architect, the technical ones behind them; set the MVP or first phase, success criteria, and timeline; write the engagement plan (the outcomes, deliverables, and acceptance criteria the team delivers against); and shape the SOW with PS leadership so what we sell is what we can deliver.

• Own scope and prioritization: decide what we do first and what we defer, manage scope as the engagement evolves, and continuously assess whether it still serves both the customer’s outcomes and LaunchDarkly’s interests, reshaping the plan when they diverge.

• Own the outcome from go-live, the point where the customer starts working the new way, through adoption: capture feedback, iterate, and prove the business value defined at the start.

• Change & Adoption

• Facilitate discovery and design sessions mapping release processes and visualizing “who should get a feature and when” without the technology or process on how to accomplish it. Adapt or invent new collaborative practices when a customer’s situation doesn’t fit one we already use, to turn ambiguous goals into clear, owned success plans.

• Lead and grow our change management practices: align customer teams on new ways of working, address resistance, and drive adoption so changes stick after the engagement ends. Scope the ongoing support plan and create the documentation and enablement the customer needs to sustain it.

• Executive & Growth

• Act as a trusted advisor to VP and C-level stakeholders: set expectations, present progress, risks, recommend data-driven decisions, and drive decisions quickly.

• Monitor account health and surface expansion or renewal signals; scope the next engagement as a natural outcome of delivered value.

• Offerings & Playbook (grows as our FDE engagement volume does)

• Turn what you learn across engagements into a feedback loop for our offerings: capture patterns, help shape how we package engagements and measure success, and help write the playbook, including how we bring on future hires.

• Delivery & Execution

• Run the delivery rhythm: status calls and reporting, accountability to tasks and deadlines across the engagement team, and escalation of technical or political blockers.

• Keep a running view of budget/burn against SOW and flag over/under-projection early; partner with PM-type support (where it exists on an account) for detailed tracking and change-order mechanics.

jobs.description:
Not all heroes wear capes — but plenty of them use toilet paper

Want to challenge yourself at a purpose-led scale up AND make a difference in the world? Come join the revolootion!

Funny name, serious business

We are a leading eco-friendly household essentials business and we donate 50% of our profits to help everyone gain access to clean water and a toilet. As of June 2024, we’ve contributed over $20 million AUD to this mission. Basically, we’re really good at making it easy to do good.

We operate scaling businesses the UK, US, Australia and Canada. Our amazing team is based in Australia, the UK, the Philippines, China, and the US. Our 250+ people aim to make the biggest possible impact for people and the planet. Over the next 5-10 years, we’re hoping to increase our annual donation tenfold to get us closer to our dream of everyone in the world having access to clean water and sanitation services.

A bit about the role

As our AR & AP Lead, you’ll be the eyes and ears of our Number Scrunchers accounting function — driving accounts receivable and accounts payable operations day to day, in close partnership with your two direct reports (our AR Expert and AP Coordinator) and the wider Financial Operations team. You’ll keep our books accurate, our customers paying on time, and our suppliers paid on time, all so we can maximise the donations we’re able to make.

If you worked here this past month here are some things you might have been involved in

• Pulled together the monthly AR ageing report for the CFO and exec team, with a clear plan to chase down aged amounts

• Reviewed the weekly payments file (including the Tipalti funding summary) before it went out for approval

• Flagged an “at risk” customer account early and looped in the customer-facing team for support

• Helped close the books accurately and on time at month-end, escalating one risk early to the Head of Financial Operations

• Worked with the AP Coordinator to tidy up a clunky step in the AP process

Let’s talk about you

Detail is your love language

You get real satisfaction from a reconciliation that ties out perfectly and a report that lands on the CFO’s desk without a single follow-up question. You’re equally comfortable rolling your sleeves up in the detail of a customer account and stepping back to build the KPIs and reporting that keep the whole team honest.

Calm under a closing calendar

Month-end doesn’t rattle you. You know how to keep AR and AP on track to a deadline, spot a risk early enough to actually do something about it, and communicate clearly with stakeholders when something needs to change.

A coach as much as a doer

You lead a small, tight-knit team and genuinely enjoy it — you give clear, kind feedback, help your people grow, and aren’t afraid of a difficult conversation when a process or a stakeholder relationship needs a repair job.

You give a crap.

Do you want your work to make the world a better place? Do you want to work with other people who feel the same way? What a coincidence — us too!

Why should you work with us?

First off, as a certified B Corp™, we work to make a difference every day while maintaining the high standards of social and environmental impact. We’re in very good company with other exceptional B Corps around the world.

We also believe that helping to make the world a better place should be rewarded accordingly – that’s why we offer competitive, market informed salaries, meaningful support towards healthcare for our team around the world, generous paid leave, tailored learning and development opportunities, and free toilet paper (yes, you read that right).

Our engagement surveys (thanks Culture Amp!) tell us that our team is really proud (over 90%) to work for Who Gives A Crap and, well, we couldn’t be more proud of that.

Have you made it this far?

If you’re still reading, we think there’s a strong chance you might be our kind of person. Here’s the thing, though — research suggests that 60% of women and underrepresented folks might have already talked themselves out of applying. Even if you don’t check every box above, we want to encourage you to introduce yourself. We believe a diversity of perspectives and experiences makes a team stronger — and the stronger our team, the closer we are to delivering toilets and clean water for all.

About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

• Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.

• Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.

• Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.

• Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.

• Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.

• Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.

• Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.

• Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist , NPR , TED , and The Washington Post . We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

About this role:

Are you an experienced engineer at the stage of your career where, above all, you want to do good?

This role is about using engineering to support fundraising: delighting our donors; helping our fundraisers; getting donations recorded and safely started on their journey to our recipients; telling donors and the public about what happens to their gifts. A bit of website development. A lot of plumbing.

The good news about this position:

• You will make a difference to people in extreme poverty

• You will work independently, with few constraints

• You will work directly with lovely people from across our fundraising teams

The trade-offs:

• There is only one other fundraising engineer and mostly you will be working on your own

• Our technology is a mixture of boring (Laravel, PHP, plain JS, HTML and CSS) and legacy (Salesforce, Wordpress, wrangling CSV files sent by our partners)

• We're growing, but this is a role for someone who values depth and impact over a fast title ladder.

The maybe good maybe bad news about the role depending on who you are:

If you want a role where you will be part of a bigger engineering team, working in Python or working on more complex tasks, then please take a look at our other engineering roles .

jobs.sourceName: Jobicy: latest jobs
jobs.description:
The Clover Care Services organization delivers proactive support and care to our members through our clinical Clover Home Care teams, and quality improvement services to our aligned providers through our practice engagement team. Clover has built one of the most proactive, data-driven health care services platforms and is excited about how technology impacts our ability to bring transformative results to both patients and providers.

Clover Care Services is entering a significant period of clinical growth. As we scale our Clover Care Visit (CCV) team, we need a dedicated leader who can turn an ambitious hiring plan into a reliable, repeatable workforce engine—from recruiting pipeline and onboarding capacity through clinician readiness, productivity, and performance.

As the Director, Workforce Management , you will connect workforce planning, recruiting, onboarding, leadership capacity, and performance management into one operating system, giving the organization clear visibility into whether we are on pace and what needs to change when we are not.

As Director, Workforce Management, you will:

• Own the CCV workforce plan end to end. Build and run the staffing strategy required to scale the clinician organization, translating long-range growth targets into weekly and monthly hiring, onboarding, and readiness goals.

• Create visibility from candidate pipeline to “ready to visit.” Establish the operating metrics, forecasting, and reporting needed to understand recruiting conversion, onboarding lead times, attrition, training capacity, and clinician readiness—and surface risks early enough to act.

• Build a scalable clinician onboarding model. Partner across Clinical, Talent, IT, Operations, and other teams to evolve today’s high-touch onboarding journey into a structured model that can support significantly larger hiring cohorts without sacrificing clinical quality.

• Build the leadership capacity required to scale. Determine the right model for preceptors, clinical leads, onboarding cohorts, and frontline management so that rapid growth does not create an unsustainable burden on existing clinical leaders.

• Own workforce performance management. Establish clear, actionable standards and operating rhythms across areas such as attendance, cancellation rates, Clover Assistant Touch, productivity, and normalized performance measures.

• Make quality and productivity work together. Build performance expectations that reflect accurate, sustainable clinical performance—not simply higher activity—and partner with clinical leaders to ensure workforce decisions support both member experience and quality of care.

• Turn workforce data into decisions. Build the dashboards, forecasts, and management routines leaders need to understand capacity, identify constraints, allocate resources, and stay ahead of hiring or performance gaps.

• Create repeatable workforce-management capabilities for CCS. Use the CCV ramp as the first proving ground for processes, tools, and operating models that can later support In-Home Care and other Clover Care Services programs.

• Operate as a cross-functional leader. Bring together Clinical Activation, clinical leadership, Talent, Operations, Finance, analytics, and other partners around one integrated workforce plan with clear owners, milestones, and escalation paths.

Success in this role looks like:

In your first 90 days, you will:

• Build a clear baseline of the CCV workforce funnel and translate the 2027 growth target into a measurable workforce plan spanning recruiting, onboarding, training capacity, clinician readiness, and attrition.

• Identify the biggest risks and bottlenecks in the ramp and establish the metrics, operating cadence, and accountability needed to address them.

Within your first 6 months, you will:

• Establish a predictable recruiting-to-readiness operating model, including scalable onboarding cohorts, preceptor capacity, and clinical leadership support.

• Launch workforce dashboards and performance-management routines that enable leaders to anticipate capacity gaps, manage performance, and increase clinician onboarding volume without sacrificing quality.

Over time, you will:

• Help CCV reach its clinician-capacity goals ahead of the 2027 AEP cycle through a sustainable, data-driven approach to hiring, onboarding, and performance.

• Build repeatable workforce-management capabilities that can extend beyond CCV to support In-Home Care and other Clover Care Services programs.

• You have built or led workforce planning, capacity management, clinical operations, field operations, or another complex people-scaling function where success depended on turning ambitious growth targets into an executable operating plan.

jobs.title: Design Engineer - Canada
jobs.sourceName: Jobicy: latest jobs
jobs.description:
Hi 👋🏾 I’m Abhik , Ashby's Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. This role is close to my heart because, as someone who can both design and code, it’s where I’ve always done my best work, but also where I was seen as a rebel and an outsider. I want folks like me to feel at home at Ashby, and so I made Design Engineering a formal role and department that works closely with me. Our first hire was over five years ago, and we’re doubling the team from five to over ten in the next year.

This role truly expects you to design and code. Design Engineer at Ashby isn’t just a Frontend Engineer with new branding, nor is it a Designer vibe coding prototypes. Combining excellence in both is where magic happens. I found that when I put my best effort into both the design and technical implementation of a feature, I had a nimbleness and creativity that was hard to achieve when I did only one or the other. For instance, the UX and UI I envisioned often influenced the data model's design and flexibility, while the understanding of technology's capabilities often simplified or improved the design. This role embraces that.

You’ll work on our most challenging design problems, help others improve their designs by expanding and enhancing our in-house design system, and consult on bespoke design work needed by Product Engineers. To ground it with examples, Design Engineers at Ashby have:

•
Redesigned our mobile web app by talking with customers who use it often, wireframing new flows, implementing its design system, and using that system to turn the wireframes into a polished UI.

•
Built a set of flexible, composable components in our design system that allow other engineers to build beautiful, consistent setup wizards across our product easily.

•
Helped a Product Engineer improve the information hierarchy and scannability of their design for viewing a candidate’s assessments. Recruiters can quickly parse information and pick out anomalies.

The Design Engineer role is more common today than five years ago, but I believe Ashby offers a unique opportunity that few can match:

•
You work on a product at scale, not at an early-stage startup struggling to find users and get feedback on what you’ve designed and built. At Ashby, your work will touch over 100,000 weekly active users, millions of candidates per week, and notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. You’ll get to test out ideas with our own recruiting team and hiring managers who use Ashby every day (like me), and often hear customer feedback as early as the day you release.

•
This role has always had the commitment of both Benji (CEO & Co-Founder) and me: I’ve held the role, steadfastly championed it since we started hiring in 2020, and haven’t diluted its responsibilities as we’ve grown (in fact, we’ve doubled down).

•
You get to shape the UI and UX of a powerful and complex product. Our users need software that helps them move quickly while adapting to their unique workflows and preferences. As a result, our UI isn’t a simple chatbox, but it can’t rely on a sea of knobs and dials either. It needs to feel approachable to someone using it for the first time while offering increasingly powerful ways to customize and automate their work.

Why You Shouldn’t Apply

Design Engineers come in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. Here are some reasons you might not enjoy the role:

•
You only want to work on design systems . While improving our design system is one of many responsibilities, you won’t be able to work on it exclusively.

•
You like to do extensive research and user testing before implementation. The beauty of being part-Engineer is that you can build conviction by shipping to a subset of users (including our own team) and gathering feedback!

•
You want everything to be perfect before it gets into a user’s hands. One of the drivers of our success is that we ship fast . While we appreciate the strive for perfection, we also realize it doesn’t need to be achieved all at once; instead, we iterate over time, often letting user feedback and business needs drive prioritization.

•
You don’t have excellent taste and execution in visual design. Design Engineers set the bar for visual design in our app and continually improve it, pushing its boundaries with each new feature or redesign.

•
You need company-driven process and structure to get your projects across the finish line. Sprint planning and well-defined project management processes are things you need or look to others to lead. You’d rather focus on the design and technical details.

•
You only want to do exciting work. We’re building a team of kind, collaborative folks. Customer issues and investigations are distributed across the team, including our high-level ICs.

What Seniority/Level To Apply For

We’ve posted levels from Junior to Staff. The higher the level, the more experience and alignment with the role we expect when reviewing your application and while interviewing. Please

In August 2026 MaintainX became part of Autodesk, joining Autodesk Operations Solutions , the organization unifying Autodesk's operations platform alongside Tandem, FlexSim and Fusion Operations. jobs.description:
What We Do:

Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

Huntress now secures more than 6M endpoints and 16M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

Reports to: Director, Engineering
Location: Remote US, Only
Compensation: $215,000 to $240,000 base plus bonus and equity

What You’ll Do:

Huntress is building an Agentic SOC. When our detection pipeline raises a signal, an LLM-based agent picks it up and investigates it end-to-end. It gathers telemetry across our products, reconstructs what happened, and makes a well-documented determination about whether the activity is malicious. Over time, it will take on more of the work itself, growing from resolving routine cases to acting fast when it finds an attack and handing analysts cases with the evidence already assembled. We’re hiring a Principal Software Engineer to head this effort.

This system is meant to augment our analysts, not replace them. It takes the high-volume, repetitive work off their plates so they can focus on complex cases and hands-on keyboard intrusions where human expertise matters most. It also reduces toil in the rest of their day by using LLMs to pre-process the output of the tools analysts use constantly, so they start from a clear picture instead of raw telemetry.

This isn’t a chatbot bolted onto a dashboard. The system investigates a large volume of signals a day across thousands of customer organizations. Many signals are benign, but some are live intrusions where minutes matter. The telemetry the system reads comes from environments in which attackers are actively operating. Because the system makes real decisions, like closing an investigation or isolating a host, it has to be right, it has to show its work, and it has to know when to hand off to a person.

As the technical lead, you’ll own the system’s architecture and direction. That means deciding how an investigation is structured, where deterministic code ends and model reasoning begins, what the agent can and can’t touch, how we know it’s working, and which decisions it makes on its own as it proves itself. You’ll work closely with SOC analysts, detection engineers, product, and other engineering teams. You’ll go deep in the code and help the engineers around you grow. Your work will directly shape how Huntress scales protection for the 99% .

We make full use of AI coding tools to enable you to accelerate your development. We don’t cap token usage. We expect you to use AI and all tools responsibly.

Responsibilities:

• Own the architecture of agentic investigation. You help define how signals move from detection into investigation, how investigation state is managed, how tools are designed and exposed to agents, and what a finished investigation contains: the verdict, the timeline, the scope, and the evidence behind every claim. When the team is stuck between options, you make the call, and the foundations you set are what others build on for years.

• Build agents that investigate like a strong analyst. You work alongside our SOC and product researchers to learn how experienced analysts actually triage and investigate, then turn that into agent behavior: which questions to ask, which evidence to gather, when to dig deeper, and when to stop and hand off to a human.

• Take toil off analysts’ plates. Beyond full investigations, you build LLM-powered pre-processing for the tools and data sources analysts rely on every day. It summarizes, correlates, and highlights what matters, so analysts spend their time on judgment instead of assembly.

• Bring a security mindset to the agent itself. The agent reads attacker-influenced data, runs across thousands of customer tenants, and can take action in customer environments. You design as if someone is trying to manipulate it, because someone will. Trust boundaries, tenant isolation, and auditability are part of the architecture from the start.

Distributed across 200+ public data centers globally and thousands of private sites at the edge, the SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange is the world’s largest in-line cloud security platform.

Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

About the Role

The AI revolution is here, and enterprises are racing to adopt GenAI - but they cannot deploy what they cannot secure. Zscaler is seeking an experienced Principal AI Security Specialist to bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI innovation and robust enterprise security.

In this highly strategic, field-facing role, you will combine the elite consultative strengths of a Solutions Engineer with deep expertise in LLMs, RAG architectures, and data protection. As our premier technical authority, you will partner with Fortune 500 executives and architects, serving as a trusted advisor to help them confidently unlock the power of AI without compromising their data or infrastructure. If you are a builder, an educator, and a master storyteller who thrives in a fast-evolving market, this is your chance to lead the industry's most critical conversation.

When needed, take customers through successful demos and POVs to validate Zscaler’s ability to securely enable enterprise AI.

• Serve as a Subject Matter Expert: Act as the field authority on modern AI patterns (such as RAG, agents, and prompt workflows), advising clients on how to prevent sensitive data exposure and unsanctioned AI usage.

• Scale the Field Motion: Collaborate with Product and Engineering to inject real-world customer feedback into the product roadmap, while building reusable demo assets and enablement playbooks to upscale our global sales force.

• You are customer-obsessed. You build deep empathy for the customer—both internal and external—and anchor your decisions in solving their real-world problems. You champion their needs from start to finish, knowing their success is our success.

• You are driven by innovation. You have a deep curiosity for how things work and are energized by solving complex technical challenges. You believe in the power of technology to accelerate transformation and are always looking for a better, more secure, and scalable way.

What We’re Looking For

• Deep Fluency in AI/GenAI: Strong foundational knowledge of Large Language Models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), MCP (Model Context Protocol) orchestration patterns, and the inherent security risks associated with them.

What is PerfectServe?

PerfectServe is a leading provider of clinical communication and physician scheduling solutions in the health IT space. The company was founded in 1997 and has grown steadily since then, with a notable jump after several major acquisitions were announced in 2019. PerfectServe now has 400+ employees, 30,000+ customers — spanning medical practices, hospitals, and health systems — and $100 million+ in annual revenue.

PerfectServe’s mission is to accelerate speed to care by optimizing provider schedules and routing communications — including messages, pages, calls, and alerts — to the right place at the right time in any care setting. By facilitating real-time information sharing, building better schedules, and automating important clinical workflows, we believe we can help our customers advance patient care and improve the well-being of their clinicians.

Leading analyst firms like Gartner® and KLAS Research have consistently validated our approach:

• In 2026, PerfectServe was named highest in execution and furthest in vision in the Gartner Magic Quadrant™ for Clinical Communication and Collaboration — the clear segment leader.

At PerfectServe, you'll have a unique opportunity to join a collaborative team with decades of experience that finds new ways to delight our customers every day. This involves consistent efforts to stay on the cutting edge of product development, which includes everything from implementing AI in new and existing solutions to brainstorming with customers about novel workflows. But you don't have to be in product to make in impact — everybody at PerfectServe contributes to important work that moves the business forward.

If you're looking for a well-established, tech-forward company full of smart people doing meaningful work, you've found the right place!

About the role

PerfectServe is investing in a unified data platform spanning our product portfolio — the data store, the shared taxonomy, and the pipelines that will let the business answer questions across the whole platform. Our architecture team has mapped the high-level direction and target state. The detailed design is deliberately still open.

This is the senior engineering seat that takes it from direction to working platform. You will shape the detailed architecture alongside our architecture team, own the implementation and integration design, and set the engineering standards the team works to — building it with a dedicated team.

Why this role, specifically

We have done real thinking here — the high-level direction and target state are mapped, and the business case is made and funded. What is deliberately not settled is almost everything below that line. We would rather hire someone with strong opinions about it than fill it in ourselves before you arrive.

That is where the consequential decisions live — how entities resolve consistently across a broad portfolio, how time is modeled so a question about last quarter resolves against last quarter's reality, how a metric gets defined once and trusted everywhere. Cheap to get right now, expensive to correct later.

So you get a direction to work from and an architecture team to partner with, plus genuine influence over both. If you would rather bring your experience to bear on a platform while it is being built than inherit one that is already set, this is that role.

What you will do

• Own the implementation design across the platform — ingestion, modeling, and the surfaces people consume

• Shape the detailed architecture from the high-level direction, working with our architecture team

• Own integration design across a varied set of production source systems

• Build ingestion pipelines from those systems

• Model raw data into business-ready datasets, with one agreed definition per metric

• Set the engineering standards the team works to, including data quality and testing

• Partner with our platform and operations teams on safe, low-impact extraction from production databases

• Work directly with the people who need the data, so what gets built answers real questions

• Mentor data engineers and help shape their work

What you bring

• Substantial experience building and operating cloud data platforms, ideally including one you designed from scratch

• Comfort making decisions with incomplete information, and the judgement to know which ones are expensive to get wrong

• A transformation framework such as dbt, with clear opinions on how to structure a project

Who We Are

Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too.

We’re building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow’s machine learning open source and hosted tools. That includes counting cells to accelerate cancer research, improving construction site safety , digitizing floor plans , preserving coral reef populations , guiding drone flight , and much more .

Roboflow is supported by great customers and investors, having raised over 63 million from Y Combinator, Google Ventures, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors.

Roboflowers are passionate builders who value ownership, accountability, and a bias toward action. We're curious, hands-on with new tech, and prefer showing our work over talking about it. Many of us have a founder mindset and thrive in our high-autonomy environment.

What You'll Do

You'll be tasked with a wide range of projects. Each engineer has a realm they focus on, but we're still small enough that we don't have the luxury of deep specialization. We're looking for technical generalists that aren’t afraid to dive into a new stack or toolchain if the need arises (but JavaScript and Node.js make up the brunt of the existing codebase).

Most of the things we work on are parts of the core product (which is an end-to-end pipeline for building computer vision projects spanning from image ingestion to annotation to training and deployment) but from time to time we're also working on things like integrating marketing and sales tools, fighting fires, automating internal processes, and open source projects.

You'll have a wide degree of freedom to advocate for which projects you think should be highest priority and will contribute to our strategy decisions. If you need a rigid list of tasks spelled out in a multi-month roadmap, this role probably won't be a good fit.

The majority of our codebase is written in JavaScript, our machine learning and image processing pipeline is in Python. We run primarily on Firebase and GCS, with some machine learning infrastructure on AWS. We're increasingly using Docker (both internally and for customer facing products like our edge inference server). A lot of our code runs in the browser (including some Tensorflow JS) but we're also working on building APIs and client libraries in several languages.

You certainly don't need to be experienced in all of these areas; but should be excited to learn new skill sets as you need them. We also hope you'll bring some new knowledge and experiences you can share to help level-up the rest of the team.

We’re especially keen to add some rigor to our processes and build the foundation for rapidly scaling the engineering organization (for example: we currently have limited tests and are not using an opinionated front-end framework -- things that will need to change over the coming months in order to be able to seamlessly expand the team).

Example Projects

•
Creating a filtering interface so our users can mix and match their images based on metadata like the time of day they were captured, the GPS location, or custom tags they've applied.

•
Expanding our annotation tool to support new functionality (like polygonal annotations image segmentation).

•
Integrating the core app with external APIs for things like outsourcing annotation tasks and analyzing deployed model performance.

•
Streamlining our onboarding flow.

•
Deeper integrations with our other products like Roboflow Universe and our REST API.

•
Next-generation model assisted labeling.

•
Optimizing speed and scalability.

Who You'll Be Working With

Our team of ~120 attracts talent like executives that wanted to return to building, founders with a 100M+ exit, Roboflow users turned team members, open source contributors, a cyclist who biked across the United States, prolific high school hackers, a CTO from 100+ engineering organization, amongst many exceptional others.

You will directly be working with our Engineering Lead and a team of Full Stack Engineers.

Where You'll Work

Roboflow is fully distributed. We currently have Hubs in New York City and San Francisco (and plan to open more as we grow density in new cities). We provide opportunities (like team onsites in different cities) and resources (like a $4000/yr travel stipend) to work in person with other team members as much as you'd like, while also supporting remote team members. You can work from one of our Hubs (we offer a relocation bonus), work from home, work at co-working spaces, etc. We want you to work where you work best!

When You'll Work

Roboflow primarily operates during the daytime hours in the US and there are some synchronous meetings

Our team is committed to enhancing physician and patient quality of life through Elation, a SaaS cloud-based clinical platform. Since inception, we've been focused on building a delightful, world-class experience that empowers physicians to deliver phenomenal care to patients.

Customer support has been the same job for twenty years: a queue, a ticket, an SLA, a closed case. That's ending, fast. Over the next 6–9 months, AI will take on more of the routine, repetitive cases at Elation. That doesn't shrink the human role — it builds on it. The work becomes product intelligence: shaping how AI handles conversations, holding the customer-trust moments that need real judgment, and turning patterns into priorities Engineering delivers.

We're hiring Technical Support Specialists to anchor that shift: people who don't just close tickets, but build the systems that eliminate them, design how AI handles conversations, and turn customer patterns into product priorities.

You might’ve been the person on a team who builds the dashboards, automations, or workflows that make everyone else better from a Support, Implementation, CS Ops, or Analyst seat. Now you want to formalize that work as the role itself. As a Technical Support Specialist, you'll bring empathy and judgment to the cases that need it most, own the quality of AI-driven solutions in your domain, and synthesize patterns that influence Product and Engineering roadmaps. We hire for judgment, taste, and curiosity, not process adherence. The bar isn't how many cases you closed ; it's how much you reshaped the conditions under which cases happen .

Role and Responsibilities

• Use Good Judgment to Solve Cases. Own customer escalations with cases that genuinely require seasoned judgment, the ones AI can't safely close. Build and protect customer trust in moments that matter.

• Build and own AI quality. Configure AI within Elation's stack (intents, knowledge sources, escalation rules), build lightweight external automations, and own the quality of AI outputs in your domain.

• Synthesize and partner with Product/Eng. Produce formal weekly and monthly insights, participate in roadmap conversations with Product Development teams, and mentor Associates on their build and synthesis work.

What success looks like in your first 6 months

• Shipped 3–5 AI solutions

• A monthly drumbeat of synthesized insights that Product and Engineering act on, with visible impact on customer experience or a measurable drop in case volume

• Owns a measurable case-volume reduction in your domain by making cases not happen, not by closing them faster

• You question default workflows instead of just executing them, and you ship more by removing work, not just doing more of it.

• You build with AI to make yourself and the teammates around you faster — automating triage, drafting responses, prototyping internal tools, and turning one-off builds into reusable patterns Associates can run with .

• Mentors Associate teammates on AI builds and pattern synthesis

Professional Qualifications

• Curiosity and natural problem-solving instincts

• An instinct to raise the bar for the teammates around you — teaching others to build and synthesize, not just modeling it yourself

When a customer experiences friction, whether a delayed delivery, a subscription billing question, or a public escalation, this role turns a frustrated buyer back into a loyal brand advocate.

The Role
Standard customer support reacts to incoming tickets. As Executive Resolution & Outbound Retention Specialist, you prevent churn and protect brand reputation. Sitting inside our Outbound, Retention & Reputation team, you are the senior voice customers speak with when high-priority issues arise, and the proactive specialist who reaches out by phone and email to recover failed payments, retain subscribers, and grow verified 5-star reviews.

Outbound Retention, Payment Recovery & Reputation Growth

• Subscription Save Outreach: Connect with at-risk or canceling subscribers to understand friction points and offer flexible alternatives (skips, cadence adjustments, or product swaps).

• Trustpilot Review Generation: Reach out to verified happy GODA customers via phone and email to encourage authentic 5-star reviews on Trustpilot and public storefronts.

• Escalated Email Queue: Handle sensitive email threads escalated from Inbound Customer Care involving dispute/chargeback threats, billing misunderstandings, or repeat delivery issues.

Tracking, Compliance & Root-Cause Feedback

• 100% Case Hygiene: Maintain accurate, real-time logs across Commslayer, Shopify, and the BBB resolution tracker so zero open cases fall through the cracks.

• Upstream Prevention: Tag recurring escalation drivers (carrier delays, renewal confusion, SKU defects) and share weekly insights with the CS Manager and Process Experts to fix root causes.

Must-Haves

• Proven Voice + Email Experience: 2+ years in DTC e-commerce customer support, escalations, retention, or account resolution, with strong comfort making daily outbound phone calls and writing tailored escalation emails.

• US-Overlap Availability: Able to work a full-time shift overlapping with US daytime/afternoon hours to reach US customers live by phone.

• Composed, Persuasive Communication: Clear, warm, natural English (spoken and written) with the emotional intelligence to de-escalate upset buyers without sounding scripted or defensive.

• High Follow-Through Discipline: You never mark a case finished until the resolution is confirmed by the customer and properly logged in external portals.

• Tech-Stack Fluency: Hands-on comfort working daily in e-commerce order dashboards, helpdesks, cloud VoIP dialers, and Google Sheets trackers.

Strong Advantages

• Reputation & Dispute Experience: Prior hands-on management of Better Business Bureau (BBB) complaints, Trustpilot outreach, or chargeback/dispute prevention.

• DTC Core Tools: Direct experience with Shopify, Commslayer (or Zendesk/Gorgias), Loop Returns, Aircall/RingCentral, and subscription platforms (Recharge, Skio, or Stay AI).

• Subscription Brand Background: Previous experience supporting a high-volume DTC beauty, fragrance, wellness, or personal care subscription brand.

Instant No's

• Phone Hesitation: You prefer hiding behind email macros rather than picking up the phone to speak directly with an upset customer.

• Copy-Paste Mindset: You rely on rigid policy scripts instead of listening to the customer's actual issue and tailoring the fix.

• Loose Documentation: Forgetting to update trackers or close portal responses. Accurate records protect both the customer and our brand rating.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, APAC

Bitwarden is the trusted identity security leader for millions of users worldwide, empowering enterprises, developers, and individuals to securely manage and share sensitive information anywhere. Bitwarden makes it easy for all users to extend robust security across their devices with password management, secrets management, and passwordless and passkey innovations. The company is headquartered in Santa Barbara, California. Learn more at bitwarden.com .

Bitwarden is committed to delivering the best possible experience for users when accessing and managing their sensitive information. The Customer Success team helps customers and all Bitwarden users meaningfully engage with Bitwarden products while proactively planning for user growth, service availability, and to ultimately achieve their desired outcome. Team members have excellent product knowledge, superb technical skills, stellar grammar, attention to detail, and the ability to explain complicated things simply. Success is measured in diligence, precision, transparency, and customer assessment.

Bitwarden is looking for a server and cloud enthusiast, with experience in both communicating about and deploying these technologies. You will become a Bitwarden product expert and handle business inquiries regarding our products, troubleshooting technical issues, completing systems integrations, and ensuring customer satisfaction.

This is an all-remote team and we’re looking for someone located in the APAC region.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Functioning as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for Bitwarden and the entire product portfolio

• Leading proof-of-concept trials with customers, new deployments, and/or integrations of Bitwarden containerized services

• Advising customers on industry best practices for the full stack of Bitwarden

• Working with enterprise customers to solve issues and/or look ahead to identify solutions to situations they may face in the future

• Providing superb guidance and assistance for each business prospect or customer’s implementation of Bitwarden, integration with the rest of their technology stack, and general security

• Collaborating with Sales, Engineering, and Product associates

• Assist in planning, developing, and presenting live technical product demonstrations showcasing best practices scaled to the customer’s use-case

• Document and share customer feedback from collaborative sessions to help the Bitwarden team exceed expectations

WHAT YOU BRING TO BITWARDEN

• Excellent English and grammar

• Excellent problem-solving skills (you might not know all the answers but you know how to find and communicate the solutions)

• Project planning, including collaborative and individual time management

• A passion for supporting your team members, growing together (technical ability and emotional intelligence), and sharing your knowledge with all

• A strong sense of empathy and the ability to advocate for others

• A passion for helping Bitwarden users

• Experience from a previous technical position (e.g. Systems Engineer, Implementation Engineer, DevOps Engineer, IT Infrastructure Engineer, etc). Equivalent education or demonstrable skills may be accepted

• Ability and desire to work remotely

Familiarity with several of the following areas/technologies is preferred:

• Bitwarden

• Linux, Windows, and macOS

• Docker, Kubernetes, and Podman

• NFS and CIFS

• Bash and PowerShell

• Active Directory, LDAP, Google Workspace, Azure Entra ID, Jumpcloud, Cloudflare and Okta

• GCP, AWS, and Azure

• Android and iOS

• GitHub

• NGINX

• SQL

• TCP/IP

• DNS

• HTTP

• SMTP

• SSO implementation and best practices (SAML and OpenID Connect)

• Integrating SCIM solutions

• TLS/SSL and PKI

• RESTful APIs

WHAT TO EXPECT IN THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

• Meeting with our Recruiting Manager

• Interview with Manager of Implementation Engineering

• Interview with Implementation Engineering team members

• Interview with Chief Customer Officer & VP of Customer Success

A FEW REASONS TO WORK WITH US

• Our user community loves us and we love them. Come to work each day with a sense of purpose as we bring a more secure internet experience to everyone from our friends and family to the world’s largest organizations.

• Become an expert. You’ll get immersed in the prominent technology markets of security and open source software.

• We are dedicated to building a diverse and talented team. Work remotely with motivated and supportive team members across the world.

• Learn and grow. Take on new challenges with the support of your team, and join our #growth-club to continue personal and professional development.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/bitwarden-implementation-engineer-customer-support-apac

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com .

About the Customer Engineering Team

Mixpanel's Customer Engineering teams are analytics consultants who embed themselves within our enterprise customer teams to drive business outcomes. We work with prospects and customers throughout the customer journey to understand what drives value, and serve as the technical counterpart to our Sales organisation to deliver on that value.

You will partner closely with Account Executives, Customer Value Architects, Product, Engineering, and Support to successfully roll out self-serve analytics within our customers' organisations, help manage change, execute on technical projects and services that delight our customers, and ultimately drive ROI on the customer's Mixpanel investment.

Our Customer Engineers are inquisitive, nimble, and able to clearly articulate the technical benefits and requirements of Mixpanel to developers and product managers, while also communicating the business value of our product to senior executives.

In your first month, you'll become a Mixpanel expert—both in features and functionality as well as implementation. You'll shadow customer calls and demos with current Customer Engineers and Account Executives while learning to articulate our value proposition, and be trained on Mixpanel's internal systems and tools.

Within your first three months, you'll be directly involved in deal cycles with Account Executives. You'll lead the technical qualification for customer use cases and deliver customised demos for prospects and existing customers, working directly with leadership at the prospect's organisation to understand business challenges that can be solved through an analytics platform.

You'll also work with the prospect's business and technical teams to scope and execute proof-of-concept projects to establish Mixpanel's value—including consulting on data ingestion methods, overall architecture, success criteria, and rollout strategies for analytics tools across an organisation.

Responsibilities

• Serve as a trusted technical advisor for prospects, providing strategic consultation on data architecture, governance, instrumentation, and business outcomes

• Communicate and consult effectively at all levels of the customer's organisation to earn trust and influence buying decisions

• Bridge the technical-business gap—working with senior stakeholders to define success for proofs-of-concept and ensuring successful execution and outcomes

• Leverage your Mixpanel expertise and technical/consultative skills to impart best practices throughout proof-of-concept projects

• Partner with Account Executives to drive revenue growth, serving as the key technical contact for customers

• Partner with post-sales teams to ensure that pre-sales value propositions translate into tangible post-sales results

• Develop relationships and uncover the needs of key technical stakeholders within your assigned book of business

• Be the "Voice of the Prospect" by collecting feedback from potential Mixpanel customers and sharing it with the Product team

We're Looking For Someone Who Has

• Fluency in business and conversational Spanish and English.

• The ability to communicate with stakeholders at all levels—from discussing APIs with developers to organisational efficiency with CIOs.

• A demonstrated track record of qualifying and selling technical solutions to executive stakeholders

• 6+ years of experience in a Software-as-a-Service Sales Engineering or related role

• Familiarity with databases and cloud data warehouses (e.g., Google Cloud, Amazon Redshift, Microsoft Azure, Snowflake, Databricks)

• A successful record of experience in sales engineering, consulting, or technical project management

• Excellent written, analytical, communication, and presentation skills

• Strong process and project delivery discipline

• Proficiency with AI tools such as Claude, Claude Code, Gemini

• The ability to travel as needed

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About MetaMask

MetaMask is building a future where users can unlock the full product stack through a single, seamless identity experience, enabling access to all features with trust, safety, and minimal friction.

Today, identity verification is fragmented across several product and onboarding experiences. Users are repeatedly asked to verify themselves across different services, creating unnecessary friction, inconsistent outcomes, and degraded trust.

Universal KYC (UKYC) is a new initiative to solve this problem by creating a single, reusable identity layer across MetaMask. At the centre of this is MetaMask Passport , a product designed to enable users to verify once and unlock multiple experiences across the MetaMask ecosystem.

This role sits at the intersection of platform and product experience . You will define the primitives, standards, and user journeys that make identity verification seamless, privacy-conscious, and globally compliant.

What you’ll do

You will own the vision and roadmap for Universal KYC and MetaMask Passport, defining how a reusable identity layer unlocks the broader MetaMask product stack. You will build the underlying identity platform, creating scalable verification primitives and standards that can be adopted across products. In parallel, you will design a seamless, low-friction KYC experience that reduces time-to-first-transaction while maintaining compliance integrity. You will drive adoption across MetaMask by partnering closely with internal teams to integrate a consistent identity layer, while balancing privacy, trust, and global regulatory requirements. Throughout, you will lead execution end-to-end, aligning cross-functional teams and delivering measurable outcomes.

What we are looking for:

• Proven experience building or scaling identity verification (IDV), KYC, or onboarding products

• Strong background in fintech , ideally with exposure to Web3

• Hands-on experience working with identity verification providers (IDV vendors) such as Sumsub, Veriff, Onfido, Persona, or Stripe Identity

• Familiarity with compliance workflows , including KYC, KYB, and customer due diligence (CDD) processes

• Track record of delivering platform products adopted across multiple teams

• Ability to operate across both technical systems and user experience

What Success looks like:

• Increased KYC completion rates and reduced onboarding friction

• Reduced time-to-first-transaction across KYC-gated flows

• Increased reuse of verified identity across products

• Improved transaction success rate through consistent verification outcomes

• Strong user trust with minimal friction and compliant execution

Attributes that will make you stand out

• First-principles thinker with strong product judgment

• Deep user empathy with a focus on reducing friction and cognitive load

• Strong understanding of trust, privacy, and compliance trade-offs

• Clear, structured communicator who drives alignment and momentum

• High ownership and ability to operate in ambiguity

Why This Role Matters

Universal KYC is a foundational unlock for MetaMask, enabling users to move from fragmented, repetitive identity verification to a seamless, reusable experience across the entire product stack. It establishes a scalable, privacy-conscious identity layer that strengthens user trust while meeting global compliance requirements. This is a high-leverage role at the intersection of access, trust, and growth, critical to unlocking the next phase of MetaMask’s evolution.

Don't meet all the requirements? Don't sweat it. We’re passionate about building a diverse team of humans and as such, if you think you've got what it takes for our chaotic-but-fun, remote-friendly, start-up environment—apply anyway, detailing your relevant transferable skills in your cover letter. Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. We aim to grow this to hundreds of millions per second, and it's critical that as we grow, we improve our performance, increase our reliability, and do it efficiently and securely.

The group provisions and operates Kubernetes clusters and CSP resources across GCP, AWS, and Azure; enforces identity, access, and security controls across those environments; and runs the observability and cost-visibility systems that keep the infrastructure measurable and accountable.

You'll lead one of the squads of platform engineers that comprise the group.

We're platform engineers, and our application teams are our users. Our job is to give them leverage: self-service building blocks that take care of the hard parts of infrastructure, so they can focus on what they're building. We treat the platform as a product and value the experience of the people who use it. At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. What You’ll Do

• Shape the engineering organization standards around observability.

• Own and evolve the observability platform, including distributed logging, metrics, and tracing infrastructure.

• Build AI-native capabilities to automatically detect anomalies, diagnose failures, and accelerate root cause analysis.

• Create powerful developer experiences through dashboards, notebooks, and interactive debugging tools.

• Drive reliability automation with intelligent alerting, diagnostics, and incident response systems.

• Experience operating large scale distributed systems in production, especially logging platforms or time series databases.

• Strong fundamentals in systems, networking, and cloud infrastructure such as Kubernetes and AWS.

• Product mindset or full stack instincts and excited to build real tools engineers love to use.

• Strong communicator who can align technical and non technical stakeholders.

• Bonus if you have built or contributed to observability ecosystems such as OpenTelemetry or Prometheus

Required Experience

• Have 8+ years of relevant industry experience building and operating large-scale observability or monitoring infrastructure

• Experience implementing or operating observability platforms such as Datadog, Sentry, Splunk, or similar.

• Have strong proficiency in at least one of Ruby, Python, or TypeScript.

Preferred Experience

• Infrastructure-as-Code, such as Terraform or Crossplane.

• Container orchestration, such as Kubernetes.

• Linux systems knowledge and shell proficiency.

• Experience designing highly available and scalable systems.

Our cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $183,000-$200,000 /yr in Denver & most remote locations, and $222,000-$245,000 /yr for San Francisco, Seattle & New York. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

* Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, based in Poland, you'll build backend systems that help GitLab engineers trust the software they create with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but passing tests don't always mean the software works as intended. You'll contribute to validation approaches and feedback mechanisms that help agents catch that gap and self-correct while they work.

This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We’re looking for someone who has built with agents, run into the gap between passing tests and working software, and wants to help close it.

What you’ll do

• Own backend features from design through production rollout, making the design calls within the architecture the team agrees on.

• Build agentic code-review and validation workflows that check whether generated code does what was intended, not just whether its tests pass.

• Prototype focused validation and feedback mechanisms with your teammates, and use what you learn to improve the platform.

• Develop language-aware validation approaches, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, adapting techniques to each language while applying a shared definition of trusted software to assess whether agent-generated code delivers the intended behavior.

• Implement feedback that helps agents identify problems and self-correct during development.

• Collaborate with engineering teams to test these approaches in real workflows, measure adoption, engineer trust, and validation quality, and use those measurements to evaluate improvements.

• Participate in code and design reviews, explain implementation trade-offs, and seek feedback on your work.

• Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

• Hands-on experience building software with artificial intelligence agents and understanding why their output can pass tests yet fail to behave as intended, from encountering that gap yourself or building something to prevent it.

• Backend development experience in at least one of Rust, Ruby, Go, or Python, with openness to working across languages.

• Experience taking backend features from design into production, discussing implementation trade-offs, and knowing when to ask for guidance.

• Comfort working inside a large existing codebase, not only on greenfield projects.

• A practical approach to prototyping, learning from results, and turning useful ideas into working software.

• Clear written communication and the ability to collaborate in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.

• The ability to share decisions transparently and improve your work through iteration and feedback.

• Familiarity with containerized services; Kubernetes experience is a plus.

About the team

The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our engineers rely on every day. We work across engineering teams and programming languages to understand how people use agents, test new approaches in real workflows, and create a shared model of trusted agentic development that teams choose to adopt.

About Pinterest:

At Pinterest, AI isn't just a feature, it's a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.

Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here .

The Responsible AI team is part of the Advanced Technologies Group (ATG), Pinterest’s advanced machine learning team. ATG’s goal is to keep Pinterest at the forefront of machine learning technology across multiple use cases including recommendations, ranking, content understanding, and more. It is an applied team that works horizontally across the company on state of the art AI and ML and works on directly bringing that technology to the product in collaboration with product engineering teams. The team also publishes its work in applied research conferences, but the main goal of the team is to have a direct impact on business metrics.

At Pinterest our goal is to inspire pinners (our users) to live the life they love. The product is powered by state of the art ML algorithms which are used to understand both the billions of visually rich items on the platform and the interests of our 535M+ monthly active users and recommend inspiring personalized content to them. What this means is that ML at Pinterest is not only multi-modal utilizing image, text, and graph signals as input, but it needs to operate at a very large scale and often in a real time interactive user experience.

Pinterest is known for being a positive and inspirational place on the internet and we believe that inspiration begins with representation and belonging. The Responsible AI team is a horizontal team that collaborates across the company on various initiatives. jobs.description:
